title: ESXi Host Coredump Configuration
exclusions: Compares each governed ESXi host's newest complete coredump-target observation with explicit host policy. It covers active/configured VMFS dump files, diagnostic partitions, and network coredump enablement/check state; it does not reduce the model to only network or partition targets. Broadcom documents that ESXi 7.0 installation/upgrade commonly configures a coredump file on ESX-OSData, so a host without network/partition can still have a valid file target. A configured or reachable target does not prove a future purple diagnostic screen will occur, its dump will complete, remain untruncated, be retained, be retrievable, contain root cause, or satisfy support/privacy requirements. The rule does not validate free capacity, dump sizing, collector retention/disk, encryption, alternate targets, actual dump artifacts, support bundles, guest dumps, or hardware NMI behavior except as separate evidence. Missing/partial/stale polls and unsupported command output are health defects. No target is created, enabled, removed, tested destructively, or reconfigured.
evidence: After deployment retain governed host/build/boot/storage/diskless and target-policy inventory; exact `vmware_esxi_coredump_policy.csv` revision/hash/approval; collector code/hash and VCF PowerCLI/ESXCLI/ESXi/vCenter/Splunk versions; privileges; effective scripted-input/JSON configuration; raw `system coredump file/partition/network` outputs and normalized complete snapshots; network collector service/listener/storage/retention health; expected-host, command-layout, target-count, duplicate, timestamp, and freshness health; `vmware_esxi_coredump_configuration_health` definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch/results/delivery/disposition; approved nonproduction network check/control output; actual dump/retrieval/support evidence where available; and dated no-target, file-only, partition-only, network-only/check-fail, policy, stale, and duplicate tests. Preserve target paths/identifiers, counts, network endpoint/interface/port/check, policy, host/source versions, snapshot, and change. This documentation-only review created no ESXCLI poll, event, dump, network check, alert, or production validation evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: At fixed time ingest a complete latest host snapshot with zero active dump files, zero active partitions, network_enabled=false, and policy requiring any target; expect `no_active_coredump_target`. Ingest another with one active local file, network_enabled=true, network_check_passed=false, and policy requiring a working network target; expect only `network_target_check_failed`. Ingest a partition-only host whose policy requires local target and expect no finding. Assert counts, booleans, endpoint context, policy, snapshot, and UC ID.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows when at least one active target satisfies policy and any enabled/required network target passes its qualified check; for file-only ESXi 7+ when policy allows local; and when an older no-target row is superseded by a newer valid snapshot. Reject invalid booleans, negative counts, blank host/snapshot identity, failed/partial status, stale/future snapshots, unsupported command schema, and duplicate delivery. Separate health must expose expected host missing, conflicting/missing policy, collector command failure, and stale inventory.

dataSources: A reviewed VCF PowerCLI collector uses `Get-EsxCli -V2` and the supported `system coredump file list/get`, `partition list/get`, and `network get/check` namespaces for each governed ESXi host. It emits one normalized JSON event per host per complete daily snapshot to local `index=vmware`, `sourcetype=vmware:esxi_coredump_state`: `vcenter`, `host_moid`, `host`, integer `active_file_target_count`, optional canonical file paths, integer `active_partition_target_count`, optional partition IDs, booleans `network_enabled` and `network_check_passed` (null only when network disabled), optional network interface/server/port, `esxi_version`, `collector_schema_version`, integer `snapshot_epoch`, unique `snapshot_id`, and `collector_status=ok`. `vmware_esxi_coredump_policy.csv` states whether any, local, or network target is required. VMware Splunk add-ons do not document this source.
app: A locally maintained `TA_vmware_esxi_coredump_inventory` with reviewed VCF PowerCLI/ESXCLI V2 collector and JSON source type, plus an observability app for policy/coverage/collector and network-dump-server health, saved search, dashboard, tests, routing, and runbook. Universal Forwarder may forward collector output but is a Splunk product, not Splunkbase app 617.
spl:
index=vmware sourcetype="vmware:esxi_coredump_state" collector_status="ok" earliest=-36h
| eval vcenter=lower(trim(vcenter)), host_moid=trim(host_moid), esxi_host=lower(trim(host)), active_file_target_count=tonumber(active_file_target_count), active_partition_target_count=tonumber(active_partition_target_count), network_enabled=lower(trim(tostring(network_enabled))), network_check_passed=lower(trim(tostring(network_check_passed))), snapshot_epoch=tonumber(snapshot_epoch), snapshot_id=trim(snapshot_id)
| where len(vcenter)>0 AND len(host_moid)>0 AND len(esxi_host)>0 AND active_file_target_count>=0 AND active_partition_target_count>=0 AND in(network_enabled,"true","false") AND ((network_enabled="false" AND (isnull(network_check_passed) OR network_check_passed="")) OR (network_enabled="true" AND in(network_check_passed,"true","false"))) AND isnotnull(snapshot_epoch) AND len(snapshot_id)>0
| sort 0 vcenter host_moid -snapshot_epoch -_indextime
| dedup vcenter host_moid
| eval snapshot_age_seconds=now()-snapshot_epoch
| where snapshot_age_seconds>=0 AND snapshot_age_seconds<=129600
| lookup vmware_esxi_coredump_policy.csv vcenter host_moid OUTPUT require_any_target require_local_target require_network_target policy_id policy_version owner valid_from_epoch valid_until_epoch
| eval require_any_target=lower(trim(tostring(require_any_target))), require_local_target=lower(trim(tostring(require_local_target))), require_network_target=lower(trim(tostring(require_network_target))), valid_from_epoch=tonumber(valid_from_epoch), valid_until_epoch=tonumber(valid_until_epoch)
| where in(require_any_target,"true","false") AND in(require_local_target,"true","false") AND in(require_network_target,"true","false") AND (isnull(valid_from_epoch) OR valid_from_epoch<=now()) AND (isnull(valid_until_epoch) OR valid_until_epoch>now())
| eval has_local_target=if(active_file_target_count+active_partition_target_count>0,"true","false"), has_any_target=if(has_local_target="true" OR network_enabled="true","true","false")
| eval finding_reasons=mvappend(if(require_any_target="true" AND has_any_target="false","no_active_coredump_target",null()),if(require_local_target="true" AND has_local_target="false","required_local_target_missing",null()),if(require_network_target="true" AND network_enabled="false","required_network_target_missing",null()),if(network_enabled="true" AND network_check_passed="false","network_target_check_failed",null()))
| where mvcount(finding_reasons)>0
| eval local_severity=if(mvfind(finding_reasons,"no_active_coredump_target")>=0,"high","medium"), use_case="UC-2.1.41", observed_utc=strftime(snapshot_epoch,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table vcenter host_moid esxi_host esxi_version active_file_target_count file_targets_canonical active_partition_target_count partition_targets_canonical network_enabled network_check_passed network_interface network_server network_port has_local_target has_any_target finding_reasons local_severity collector_schema_version policy_id policy_version owner observed_utc snapshot_age_seconds snapshot_id use_case
| sort 0 -local_severity vcenter esxi_host
description: Audits ESXi coredump readiness across all documented target families: VMFS dump file, diagnostic partition, and network collector. The search selects the newest complete host observation, derives local/any target presence, applies explicit host policy, and separately reports an enabled network target whose qualified reachability check fails.
value: A VMkernel coredump can be essential for diagnosing a purple diagnostic screen, but target design differs for installed, upgraded, diskless, and constrained hosts. A complete target-family inventory prevents false alarms on valid file-backed ESXi 7+ systems while identifying hosts with no target or a failed required network path before diagnostic evidence is needed.
implementation: Deploy and qualify a daily ESXCLI V2 collector for file, partition, and network namespaces on every supported ESXi build; reject partial command sets. Govern exact per-host any/local/network requirements, save the bounded policy search, and independently monitor collector and network dump server capacity/listener/retention. Validate file-only, partition-only, and network-only designs in nonproduction, and change targets only under approved VMware/storage/network procedures.
visualization: Use a host matrix with file/partition counts and canonical identities, network enabled/check/interface/server/port, derived target state, policy, ESXi/schema version, freshness, owner, and disposition; counts by target mix/finding; and separate expected-host, command-layout, missing-policy, network-collector listener/storage/retention, actual-dump, and collector-health panels. Never label configured target as successful future dump.
schema: Purpose-built complete ESXCLI coredump file/partition/network snapshot joined to host policy
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. CIM does not preserve ESXi dump target family/identity, network check state, collector schema, complete snapshot provenance, and host-specific target policy.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is an observed target/policy condition; expected explanations still require evidence:

1. **Valid file-only ESXi 7+ design** — Broadcom documents automatic coredump files on ESX-OSData after install/upgrade. If policy allows local, zero partition/network targets is not a finding; qualify active file output.

2. **Diskless/stateless host requiring network dump** — local target can be unavailable or unsuitable. Encode network requirement explicitly and monitor collector reachability/storage.

3. **Approved target migration** — file-to-network, partition-to-file, or collector migration can create temporary overlap/gaps. Require exact hosts/targets, sequence, owner, rollback, start, and finite expiry.

4. **Configured versus active distinction** — a target can be configured for next boot but not active now. The collector must map command output correctly; policy should specify active readiness and retain configured context.

5. **Network check dependency** — receiver maintenance, path, interface, route, firewall, or collector listener can fail while a local fallback remains active. Report network failure separately and apply policy priority.

6. **Unsupported command/output version** — ESXi releases can change fields. Fail collector health rather than converting missing values to zero/false.

7. **Host maintenance/rebuild** — install/upgrade/boot-storage work can recreate or move dump files. Reconcile expected final state after the approved task.

8. **Duplicate/stale collection** — newest-snapshot selection prevents old state winning, while health must repair duplicate or delayed routes.

Suppress only exact vCenter/host/reason with owner, approved transition, start, and finite expiry. Never suppress expected-host, collector-command/schema, policy-conflict, network-collector capacity/listener, actual-dump retrieval, or source-freshness health.
mitreAttack: N/A (ESXi diagnostic-readiness monitoring; no adversary behavior asserted)
detectionType: Newest complete ESXi coredump target state fails explicit host policy
hardware: Governed ESXi hosts, including installed/upgraded hosts with ESX-OSData dump files and diskless/stateless hosts requiring an approved network dump collector.
reviewer: Source-backed documentation-only editorial review; production VMware support, storage/network, and Splunk validation pending

cost.search_load_notes: Daily one-row-per-host configuration inventory and a small policy lookup; network collector health is separate.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and target-family model

Assign VMware platform/support, boot-storage, network, dump-collector, privacy, Splunk, and change owners. Inventory every governed host by vCenter/moid, ESXi build/install history, boot mode/storage, diskless/stateless status, support requirements, active/configured file and partition targets, network collector/interface/path, target policy, and owner. Broadcom documents file, partition, and network dump mechanisms. ESXi 7.0 installation/upgrade commonly configures a file on VMFS-L ESX-OSData; do not require a partition/network universally.

Run supported VCF PowerCLI on a hardened tier with TLS to vCenter and read access needed for Get-EsxCli. Use `Get-EsxCli -V2`; Broadcom recommends V2 because V1 positional interfaces are not guaranteed compatible across ESXi versions. The Splunk role needs read/scheduled-search rights only.

## Step 1 — Collect every target family completely

Implement `TA_vmware_esxi_coredump_inventory`. For each host invoke qualified V2 methods corresponding to `system coredump file list/get`, `partition list/get`, `network get`, and, when enabled and approved, `network check`. Inspect actual V2 argument/output names per ESXi build. Count active targets separately from configured-next-boot targets and retain canonical IDs/paths in restricted fields. Record network interface, server IP, port, enabled state, and check result without inventing null=false.

Only emit `collector_status=ok` when every required namespace for that host class succeeds and maps to the versioned schema. An unsupported command, permission failure, timeout, disconnected host, or partial method set goes to a separate error source. Configure daily JSON scripted input. Compare file/partition/network output with direct ESXCLI and vSphere Client where exposed. Verify active versus configured semantics and known file-only/partition-only/network-only controls.

Create `vmware_esxi_coredump_policy.csv` keyed by vCenter/host_moid with true/false `require_any_target`, `require_local_target`, `require_network_target`, owner/version/effective dates. Preflight conflicting logic, duplicates, missing expected hosts, orphan IDs, and diskless/boot-class alignment. Independently monitor the network dump collector listener, service, destination storage/capacity/retention, firewall/path, and actual received artifacts.

## Step 2 — Create and understand the search

Save sidecar `spl` as `vmware_esxi_coredump_configuration_health` and run after collection. It validates host identity, nonnegative active counts, network/check booleans, selects newest complete host snapshot, and rejects future or >36-hour state. Exact policy supplies requirements. `has_local_target` is file count plus partition count greater than zero; `has_any_target` adds enabled network.

Reasons remain distinct: no target when any required; required local missing; required network missing; and enabled network whose qualified check failed. A failed optional network check still appears even if local fallback exists because the configured network path is unhealthy. High is reserved locally for no active target; other reasons are medium. Configuration readiness does not prove successful future dump.

Run separate health for expected hosts, command/schema support, active/configured mapping, policy duplicates/missing, collector errors, network collector service/listener/storage/retention, and actual dump/retrieval test evidence.

## Step 3 — Validate safely

Use fixtures for no target, file-only, partition-only, network-only pass/fail, local+network, active versus configured only, zero/multiple counts, network disabled/null check, invalid booleans/counts, exact/missing/duplicate/expired policy, stale/future/partial snapshots, command-layout drift, older bad/newer good, and duplicate delivery. Assert correct reasons and no assumption that partition/network is mandatory on file-backed hosts.

In nonproduction, inspect known targets and run the non-destructive `network check` only with VMware/network approval. Test collector listener/path interruption and recovery. Validate file/partition active identifiers after reboot or controlled configuration change. A deliberate purple diagnostic screen or dump generation requires a separate safety/support test plan; it is not required to validate search logic and must never be triggered in production for a routine control.

## Step 4 — Triage and remediate deliberately

Alert title should say `ESXi coredump target configuration needs review`. Include host/build/boot class, file/partition counts/IDs, network state/check/endpoint/interface, policy, source/schema health, collector health, change context, and raw links. Verify direct ESXCLI live state; confirm host policy/class; inspect active versus configured target; check target storage capacity/access; for network, verify interface/route/firewall/listener/destination/retention; review install/upgrade/maintenance changes; and classify approved transition, missing target, failed network path, policy defect, collector defect, or unresolved.

Never automatically add/remove/enable a dump file/partition, alter autoCreateDumpFile, point to a collector, change VMkernel networking/firewall, reboot, or generate a crash. Wrong storage/network changes can impair boot or diagnostics. Use approved Broadcom procedures with support, capacity, rollback, and maintenance planning. Close only when direct and fresh snapshot state satisfy policy, network collector/path is healthy if required, retrieval/retention design is approved, and evidence is retained.

## Step 5 — Troubleshoot

- **All local counts zero on ESXi 7+:** verify file-list/get command mapping, active versus configured fields, permissions, and ESX-OSData; do not infer no target from partition output alone.
- **Network enabled but check null:** collector contract is invalid; run/marshal the qualified check or mark partial unless local policy explicitly excludes check with a separate schema.
- **V2 method missing:** inspect ESXi build command namespace and `Get-EsxCli -V2` help; version the adapter and fail health.
- **Direct ESXCLI differs:** align host/vCenter, sample time, active/configured distinction, pending reboot, and collector serialization.
- **Network check fails:** inspect VMkernel interface, route, server IP/port, firewall, collector listener/service/storage, and time; local fallback does not repair network path.
- **Target exists but no actual dumps:** configuration is not proof of future success; review prior crashes, target capacity, truncation, retention, and retrieval/support workflow.
- **State changes after reboot/upgrade:** inspect smart selection, auto-created dump file, boot storage, lifecycle task, and approved final policy.

Retention and testing follow support/privacy policy. This use case monitors configuration readiness and never guarantees diagnostic capture.
grandmaExplanation: We check that each virtualization host has an approved place to save diagnostic information if it crashes. We recognize local files, special disk areas, and network collectors, but a configured destination is not a promise that a future crash report will succeed.
